summary: Introductory security posture discovery focused on whether Novella Health should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Key customer concerns: SOC 2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS control, and data residency. Redwood AE + SE explained deployment options and fallbacks; agreed to share SOC2/ISO reports, architecture diagrams, and schedule a technical deep dive for benchmarking and Private deployment requirements.
topics: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance and evidence
RBAC, roles, and least privilege best practices
Audit logging, retention, and access to logs
Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Data residency and retention policy requirements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (CISO, Novella), Ethan Park (Head of Infra), Maya Torres (DevOps)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood. Priya's our SE, she'll cover the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura Gomez: Doing good, thanks. We're trying to go through security posture, figure out whether we can use Redwood Hosted or if we need Dedicated or Private. Primary concern is PHI data residency and how keys are managed.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Great, thanks Laura. We'll walk through SOC 2/ISO, SSO and provisioning, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, and retention. Quick note: we'll share SOC2 artifacts after the call.
[00:30] Ethan Park: Quick context — we're on GCP, have a HIPAA program, strict retention windows, and some datasets must remain in us-east-1. We also use Okta for SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:42] Alex Chen: Perfect. Hosted can meet a lot of needs, but Dedicated or Private are options if you need isolated capacity or customer-managed networking. Can you describe the data flow and whether raw transcripts or PII land in storage you control?
[00:56] Maya Torres: Right now the flows push data into our processing buckets. We want to avoid provider-managed long-term storage for PHI. We prefer transient tokens and control over backups.
[01:10] Priya Singh: Understood. For Hosted, Redwood supports encryption at rest and in transit, and we rotate service-managed keys. We have Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) options for Dedicated and Private if you need KMS control or HSM backed keys.
[01:25] Laura Gomez: BYOK — does that mean we can use our Cloud KMS with Redwood services? We need key control so that we can revoke access if necessary.
[01:33] Priya Singh: Yes, for Dedicated we support customer KMS integration; for Private, you fully manage keys on your side. For Hosted there's a managed key option but we can discuss exceptions under enterprise contracts.
[01:45] Ethan Park: How about audit logs? We need file-level access logs and admin activity logs retained for two years. Can we ingest those into our SIEM?
[01:55] Alex Chen: We expose audit logs for admin actions, model deployments, and access. For Dedicated and Private, logs can be shipped to your SIEM via log forwarding or syslog; Hosted has an export and long-term retention add-on. We'll share the logging guide.
[02:08] Maya Torres: Is there support for immutable logs or WORM storage? We have compliance constraints.
[02:14] Priya Singh: We don't enforce WORM on Hosted by default, but Dedicated/Private can be configured to forward to your immutable storage. We can also sign logs and provide tamper-evidence for audit purposes.
[02:30] Laura Gomez: What about certifications? Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? Any gap letters?
[02:36] Alex Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II in scope for the hosted platform and an ISO 27001 program. We'll send the attestation and summary post-call. For Dedicated/Private, the infrastructure may require additional validation — we'll highlight scope boundaries in the report.
[02:50] Ethan Park: For SSO we use Okta. How does Redwood handle SAML and SCIM? We need automated provisioning and role sync.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. SCIM syncs groups and roles; RBAC maps to your groups. There are some edge cases with nested groups — we've seen that with Okta — but we can run a test import.
[03:12] Laura Gomez: RBAC: we need least-privilege for developers and separate access for security ops. Can we create custom roles and limit token creation?
[03:19] Priya Singh: Yes, customers can define role sets and limit credential scopes. For Dedicated and Private you can enforce stricter controls and disable some self-service flows.
[03:30] Alex Chen: Quick note about keys and tokens: we support short-lived tokens, session-bound credentials, and audit trails for token issuance. That helps reduce risk if a token leaks.
[03:45] Ethan Park: What about network controls? We require VPC peering or private link to avoid public internet egress for data in transit.
[03:53] Priya Singh: For Hosted, we offer PrivateLink/Private Service Connect in major clouds; Dedicated supports customer VPC peering with dedicated pools; Private gives you full control inside your VPC or on-prem. We'll attach our network diagram and checklist.
[04:10] Maya Torres: Latency is a concern if we go Private on-prem. We have some latency-sensitive inference flows. Could Dedicated in us-east-1 be a middle ground?
[04:20] Alex Chen: Absolutely — Dedicated gives isolation and lower latency without full on-prem maintenance. We can run throughput/latency benchmarks with your sample payloads in a POC.
[04:32] Laura Gomez: Data residency — we must ensure certain datasets never leave us-east-1. How do you guarantee region locking?
[04:40] Priya Singh: Customers can pin data and models to regions in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports region selection but not strict legal region locks unless part of enterprise contract; we'll document region isolation guarantees.
[04:55] Ethan Park: Encryption — anything about HSM-backed keys? We prefer HSM-backed customer keys for the most sensitive data.
[05:03] Priya Singh: We offer HSM-backed BYOK for Dedicated and Private; the Hosted offering uses cloud KMS with FIPS 140-2 modules in supported clouds. Again we'll include the key management whitepaper.
[05:18] Alex Chen: Can we talk about retention? What are your retention windows and purge requirements?
[05:24] Laura Gomez: We have a default 30-day window for intermediate artifacts, but regulated datasets require 7-year retention for audit logs. We also need guaranteed purge for derivatives within 72 hours unless archived.
[05:36] Priya Singh: We can set retention policies per workspace and per dataset. For Hosted, retention is configurable but archiving to customer-managed buckets is recommended for long-term retention. Dedicated/Private can adhere to your retention and purge SLAs.
[05:52] Ethan Park: Is there a way to prevent model caching of user data to avoid leakage into model weights or shared caches?
[05:59] Priya Singh: Great question. We have KV cache and prefix caching controls. For sensitive workloads you can disable caching, enable strict prefix isolation, and route requests to private pools. We also support model variants that don't store prompts in long-term caches.
[06:18] Maya Torres: How do you handle backups and snapshots for Private deployments? We need encryption and the ability to rotate keys and revoke access to old backups.
[06:28] Priya Singh: Backups are encrypted with your keys for Private. You manage key rotation and revocation. For Dedicated, we can configure backup targets to your encrypted buckets.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Any regulatory frameworks besides HIPAA we should be aware of that affect your choice?
[06:46] Laura Gomez: We're mostly HIPAA, some EU customers so GDPR processing agreements. Need DPA and data processing addendum. Also potential ISO evidence for vendors.
[06:55] Priya Singh: Redwood has a DPA and standard contractual clauses for EU. We'll include the DPA and vendor questionnaire responses in the packet.
[07:06] Ethan Park: From an ops perspective, what visibility do we get into the runtime — token-level usage, per-model latency breakdowns?
[07:13] Alex Chen: Redwood Console exposes per-route token usage, latency percentiles, and detailed tracing hooks. For Dedicated and Private you get more granular logs and longer retention.
[07:26] Laura Gomez: For audits, do you provide evidence packages showing access history and configuration at a point in time?
[07:33] Priya Singh: Yes — we can provide point-in-time snapshots of config, audit logs, and change history. For Dedicated/Private we can generate environment-specific evidence.
[07:45] Maya Torres: Are there any known limitations with SCIM group mapping when we have nested groups in Okta?
[07:52] Priya Singh: We sometimes see nested group flattening issues depending on the IdP. We have workarounds and scripts to normalize groups during import; we'll test in the technical deep dive.
[08:05] Alex Chen: Let's surface common objections: latency vs cost tradeoff, and control vs operational overhead. How do you weigh those?
[08:13] Ethan Park: We prefer predictable latency; we're willing to pay for Dedicated if it removes variability. Ops overhead is acceptable if security requirements demand it.
[08:22] Laura Gomez: Also need to understand incident response and breach notification timelines.
[08:27] Priya Singh: Our standard incident notification SLA is 24 hours for high-severity customer-impact incidents; we provide playbooks for forensic evidence and support. We'll share the incident response summary.
[08:40] Alex Chen: For the POC/benchmarks, what metrics should we measure? Latency p95/p99, throughput, token costs, and error rate? Anything else?
[08:48] Ethan Park: Add cold-start times and KV cache warmup behavior. Also measure across sequence lengths and batch sizes.
[08:56] Priya Singh: Noted. We'll provide a benchmark harness and recommended payloads.
[09:05] Laura Gomez: For contractual terms, we need SOC2 carve-outs and the ability to audit Dedicated infra. Can we get an on-site or remote audit access?
[09:14] Alex Chen: For Dedicated and Private customers we offer audit access and can accommodate remote evidence collection. On-site audits are handled case-by-case. We'll flag that for legal.
[09:26] Maya Torres: A couple of gotchas — token leakage from SDKs and local dev machines. Do you provide guidance?
[09:33] Priya Singh: We have developer best practices and a secrets management guide; for regulated teams we recommend limited credential issuance and rotate tokens frequently.
[09:44] Ethan Park: Anything about model ownership and kept artifacts — do Redwood-hosted models ever ingest customer prompts for training?
[09:51] Alex Chen: Redwood does not use customer prompts to train our public models. For Hosted, we may use telemetry for performance improvements but customer data is excluded from training datasets by default under enterprise contracts. We'll include the privacy policy and training data policy.
[10:06] Laura Gomez: Ok, sounds good. Can you share the SOC2 report now or is it after the call?
[10:11] Alex Chen: We'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO summary after the call; action item logged.
[10:18] Priya Singh: Anything else on compliance side — e.g., FedRAMP or specialized certifications?
[10:24] Laura Gomez: Not for us right now. We mainly need SOC2 and ISO artifacts plus the DPA.
[10:30] Alex Chen: Great. Recap: we'll share reports, network and deployment diagrams, benchmark plan, and schedule the technical deep dive. Any final questions?
[10:41] Maya Torres: One last — can you provide example retention policy configs and sample log forwarding configs?
[10:47] Priya Singh: Yes, we'll attach sample configs and the logging forwarding guide.
[10:54] Ethan Park: Appreciate it. We'll gather the data classification matrix and come back with potential PII lists.
[11:00] Laura Gomez: Thanks Alex, Priya. We'll look for the docs and coordinate scheduling.
[11:08] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet by COB tomorrow.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-phrases (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache) and speaker attribution may be approximate. Attachments referenced: SOC2_TypeII.pdf (sent post-call), ISO27001_summary.pdf, Redwood_network_diagram.pdf, private-deploy-checklist.pdf, benchmark-harness.md
